newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power futures close mostly up, Q3 PV sold.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power futures close mostly up, Q3 PV sold.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mostly higher, but a wave of late selling, particulary of third-quarter Palo Verde (PV) contracts, pushed prices down from their highs, traders said Friday.
"We rallied up nice, but then they slammed it down," said one dealer.
July PV settled 20 cents higher at $20.20 per megawatt hour (MWh), after trading as high as $20.50, while August closed up 10 cents at $23.60, compared with a high of $24.05.
April PV closed up 15 cents at its high for the day of $14.10, while May settled 10 cents higher at $14.20.
California-Oregon border (COB) contracts settled mixed on the day, with April ending 9 cents higher at $9.99.
May COB was down 2 cents at $9.88 and June was down 10 cents at $10.35.

The northwestern section of the Pacific Northwest was expected to experience very wet conditions in the next several days along with near normal temperatures, while the southeast part of the region was expected to see dry and warm weather.
In the Southwest, temperatures were projected to run four to 11 degrees F above normal across the region with little chance of precipitation.
NYMEX estimated 120 COB and 342 PV contracts traded on Friday.
